answer: Give every identity a walnut vault: a sealed canary task only its private key can open, so n clones must solve n canaries, not one copied answer. Each epoch the canary terrain shifts like a dune, forcing fresh work that cannot be replayed or shared with a clone farm. Peers run a spiral audit, re-checking earlier canaries in widening rings; when two identities fail the same canary pattern, both stakes are slashed jointly, loss growing as the square of the linked cluster. Influence scales with the square root of stake, so n clones pay n canaries plus quadratic slashing for only sqrt(n) power.
